title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E526 Euler models the transverse vibration of an elastic rod (lamina) of length a with the Euler–Bernoulli equation and separates variables: y = C sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)) Y(u), u = s/a. For the end conditions treated in this section, the mode shape on the previous page is Y(u) = e^{uω} − e^{ω(2−u)} + (1+e^{2ω}) sin uω + (1−e^{2ω}) cos uω. Checking it gives Y''(0)=0, and Y(1)=0 and Y''(1)=0 provided the frequency equation holds. So one end is free and the other is hinged (pinned). The frequency equation is tan ω = tanh ω, with ω = a/f, f^4 = bc²k, and the sound proportional to ω²c√(2gb)/(πa²).

This page locates the roots of tan ω = tanh ω.
(1) First quadrant. Euler multiplies out to compare sin ω·2cosh ω with cos ω·2sinh ω using power series: 2ω(1 + ω²/3 − ω⁴/30 …) versus 2ω(1 − ω²/3 − ω⁴/30 …). The first exceeds the second throughout 0 < ω < π/2, so there is no root there apart from ω = 0.
(2) Even quadrants. In the 2nd, 4th, 6th, … quadrants tan ω < 0 while tanh ω > 0, so there are no roots.
(3) Third quadrant (Corollary 1, §24). Since tanh ω is just below 1, ω lies just below π + π/4. Put ω = π + ϱ/2 − Φ, where ϱ is the right angle. Then tan ω = (1 − tan Φ)/(1 + tan Φ). Comparing with (1 − e^{−2ω})/(1 + e^{−2ω}) gives exactly tan Φ = e^{−2ω} = e^{−(2π + ϱ − 2Φ)}. Neglecting Φ in the exponent, tan Φ = e^{−5π/2} ≈ 1/2576. So Φ ≈ 1.3′, which is negligible, and the first root is ω ≈ 5π/4 (225°), where sin = cos = −1/√2.
The next page continues to ω ≈ (4n+1)π/4 and gives frequencies proportional to 25 : 81 : 169 : 289 …, the overtone ratio 1 : 3¼ (roughly C to G♯ plus a comma).
errors: The first-quadrant claim is supported only by truncated series. The conclusion is nevertheless true, since tan x > x > tanh x on (0, π/2).
ω = 0 is dismissed as giving 'no motion'. For a free–pinned rod it is actually the zero-frequency rigid rotation about the pin; there is no vibration, so this is harmless.
Not on this page but in the continuation: the next page says 'quartum quadrantem' for ω ≈ 2π + 45°, which should be the fifth quadrant. It also writes ϱ = π/4 where ½ϱ = π/4 is meant.
Numerics check: e^{5π/2} ≈ 2575.97, so 1/2576 is correct. The true root is 3.92660 versus 5π/4 = 3.92699; Euler's error estimate is correct.

ideas.what: Frequency equation tan ω = tanh ω for a free–hinged (equivalently, antisymmetric free–free or clamped–hinged) beam, and its root location by quadrant and sign analysis
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1740s); systematized by Rayleigh, Theory of Sound
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum (1744) treats beam vibration frequency equations; E526 itself (Acta 1779/1782); discussed in Truesdell's Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Series comparison of sin ω cosh ω and cos ω sinh ω to exclude roots in (0, π/2)
Root refinement ω = (4n+1)π/4 − Φ with the exponentially small correction tan Φ = e^{−2ω}
ideas.modern_name: asymptotic approximation of beam eigenvalues with exponentially small correction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler/D. Bernoulli; standard in Rayleigh and later engineering texts
ideas.where_published: E526; similar estimates appear in Euler's earlier elastic-curve work

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, correct root analysis of tan ω = tanh ω with the well-known asymptotic ω ≈ (4n+1)π/4. E526 is covered in Truesdell's history, and nothing on the page appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially faithful to the image.
ϱ denotes the right angle (signum anguli recti), so ½ϱ = 45°.
